Test Description: Validate default reset values and read/write behavior of GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 registers over the AHB register interface using predefined read/write masks and multiple data patterns. Non-readable or non-writable registers are skipped per masks; expected readback accounts for preserved default bits where writes are masked off.
Meta Test Description: The test verifies default values and R/W functionality for a set of GPIO registers listed in addr_array (GPIO_8..GPIO_27). It first runs chk_rst_val(): for each address i in [0..CNT-1], it skips if skip_rst_array[i]==1; if read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000, it skips as not readable. Otherwise it performs data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i]) and masks with 0xfffffffe to ignore bit0, then compares against default_value_array[i]; on mismatch increments def_fail_cnt and logs failure. Next, chk_rd_wr(): defines six patterns {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern, it writes (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]) to each address i that is not skipped (skip_array[i]==0) and is writable (write_mask_array[i]!=0). It then reads back for each address i that is not skipped, writable, and readable (read_mask_array[i]!=0) using data_rd = read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]. Expected exp_val is computed as: (data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((~write_mask_array[i]) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]). It compares data_rd with exp_val; on mismatch increments wr_fail_cnt and logs. At the end of test_case(), if def_fail_cnt>0 or wr_fail_cnt>0 calls finish(1) else finish(0). A soft_reset_chk() routine exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Default value check intentionally masks bit0 to avoid false mismatches due to input sampling behavior. Registers with read mask of 0 are treated as non-readable and skipped; registers with write mask of 0 are treated as non-writable and skipped. Expected readback preserves default bits where writes are masked off. Ensure that the iteration count matches the size of the control arrays to avoid out-of-bounds access.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Initialize the GPIO register list (GPIO_8 through GPIO_27) with associated default, read-mask, and write-mask data. 2) Default value verification: For each GPIO register that is readable and not marked to skip, read the register and compare its value (with bit0 ignored) against the documented default value. Record any mismatches. 3) Write/read verification: For each of the six data patterns, write the pattern masked by each register’s write mask to all writable, non-skipped GPIO registers; then read back the value masked by each register’s read mask and compare against the expected value computed from the written bits plus preserved default bits where writes are masked. Record any mismatches. 4) Determine pass/fail: If no default or write/read mismatches were recorded, declare PASS; otherwise, declare FAIL.
Impacted Registers: GPIO_8, GPIO_9, GPIO_10, GPIO_11, GPIO_12, GPIO_13, GPIO_14, GPIO_15, GPIO_16, GPIO_17, GPIO_18, GPIO_19, GPIO_20, GPIO_21, GPIO_22, GPIO_23, GPIO_24, GPIO_25, GPIO_26, GPIO_27
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if, for all GPIO_8–GPIO_27: (a) the default read value (with bit0 ignored) matches the documented default when readable; and (b) for each test pattern, the masked readback equals (written_bits & write_mask & read_mask) OR (preserved_default_bits & ~write_mask & read_mask). Any mismatch results in FAIL.
Meta Arrays: const unsigned long int addr_array[20]={MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8,...,MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27}; const unsigned int default_value_array[20]={GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8_DEFAULT_VAL,...,GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27_DEFAULT_VAL}; const unsigned int read_mask_array[20]={GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8_READ_MASK,...,GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27_READ_MASK}; const unsigned int write_mask_array[20]={GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8_WRITE_MASK,...,GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27_WRITE_MASK}; const unsigned int skip_array[20]={0,...,0}; const unsigned int skip_rst_array[20]={0,...,0}

Test Description: Verify that enabling negative-edge interrupts per GPIO pad (GPIO_8–GPIO_39) correctly generates an interrupt on a falling edge, sets the group status bit, and can be cleared via per-pin raw-clear and system raw status clear, with proper ISR handling.
Meta Test Description: test_case(): Optionally enable GIC IRQ 87/88. Enable system-level GPIO interrupt output via INTREN1 for GPIO0/GPIO1. Drive pad output register at 0xA0243ffc high. For i in 0..31: configure each per-pin control at (GPIO_8 + i*4) with bits (1<<20)|(1<<18)|(1<<16). For each i: wr_val=1<<i; clear group raw status by writing wr_val to RAWSTCR1; enable group interrupt output for bit i by writing wr_val to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; set int_pend=1; drive 0xA0243ffc high then ~wr_val to create a falling edge; poll with timeout until int_pend is cleared by ISR; on timeout, record error. finish(test_err). Default_IRQHandler(): local_wr=1<<i; set int_pend=0; drive 0xA0243ffc high; read per-pin register; if ((rdata & 0x1)!=0) error; if ((rdata & 0x2)!=0x0) then check group status; clear per-pin and group raw; verify cleared; clear system RAWSTCR1; clear GIC IRQ; else error.
Remarks: Requires system interrupt enable and GIC configuration. Uses external pad drive at 0xA0243ffc to generate edges.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each GPIO_8–GPIO-39 pad generates neg-edge interrupt, group status sets, and all statuses are cleared successfully with no timeouts.

Test Description: Verify that enabling positive-edge interrupts across GPIO_8–GPIO_39 generates an interrupt on a rising edge for each pad, asserts group status, and per-pin/system raw status can be cleared; ensure correct GIC/system and GPIO interactions.
Meta Test Description: test_case(): Optionally enable GIC IRQ 87/88. Enable system-level GPIO interrupt via INTREN1. Configure per-pin pos-edge detection. Set IO groups to input. Enable group interrupts. For each pad, generate a rising edge and wait for ISR; in ISR validate group status, clear per-pin raw and system RAWSTCR1, re-enable group if masked.
Remarks: Requires system interrupt configuration and GIC enable. IO control must set pads to input before edge generation.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each pad raises interrupt on rising edge, group status sets, and statuses are cleared with no timeouts.
